question: A 13-year-old girl asks for an HIV self-test kit at OPD without a parent. Can she consent on her own?
label: reason_first

blocks.text: The patient is 13 years old, so she meets the criteria for consent for HIVST .
However, since her age of consent is below 16, assisted self-testing with a trained HTS provider would be more appropriate.
A parent or legal guardian must provide verbal assent for Paediatric Oral Fluid HIVST if the child is under 16.

references: [2] Amendment to the Eswatini Integrated HIV Management Guidelines (2024), Assisted and Unassisted – WHO Definition, PDF page 9
[6] hiv-2022, Table 3.2 HIV self-testing approaches, PDF page 53
[10] hiv-2022, Table 3.1 Upholding The 5Cs, PDF page 49
message:
The patient is 13 years old, so she meets the criteria for consent for HIVST .

However, since her age of consent is below 16, assisted self-testing with a trained HTS provider would be more appropriate.

A parent or legal guardian must provide verbal assent for Paediatric Oral Fluid HIVST if the child is under 16.

Sources: [2] Amendment to the Eswatini Integrated HIV Management Guidelines (2024), Assisted and Unassisted – WHO Definition, PDF page 9; [6] hiv-2022, Table 3.2 HIV self-testing approaches, PDF page 53; [10] hiv-2022, Table 3.1 Upholding The 5Cs, PDF page 49

key_facts: 1. [id: 2] Children 12 years and above can consent for HIVST on their own.
2. [id: 5] The age of consent for HIVST in Eswatini is 16 years.

3. [id: 6] However, assisted self-testing can be offered to individuals as young as 12 years old with a trained HTS provider giving an in-person demonstration before or during HIVST on how to perform the test and interpret the test result.
4. [id: 10] For individuals under 16, verbal assent by a legal guardian is obtained for Paediatric Oral Fluid HIVST.

question: Adult outpatient newly diagnosed with HIV, CD4 is 180. Should I send serum CrAg and urine TB-LAM?
label: reason_first

blocks.text: Yes, send serum CrAg. The patient is a newly diagnosed adult with advanced HIV disease (CD4 = 180).
No, do not send urine TB-LAM. The patient has a CD4 count of 180, which is above the threshold for TB LAM testing.

references: [1] hiv-amendment-2024, Advanced HIV package, PDF page 25
[2] hiv-2022, Advanced HIV package of care, PDF page 132
[5] hiv-amendment-2024, Summary of Changes, PDF page 23
message:
Yes, send serum CrAg. The patient is a newly diagnosed adult with advanced HIV disease (CD4 = 180).

No, do not send urine TB-LAM. The patient has a CD4 count of 180, which is above the threshold for TB LAM testing.

Sources: [1] hiv-amendment-2024, Advanced HIV package, PDF page 25; [2] hiv-2022, Advanced HIV package of care, PDF page 132; [5] hiv-amendment-2024, Summary of Changes, PDF page 23

calls.name: guideline_answer

raw_blocks.text: Yes, send serum CrAg and urine TB-LAM. The patient has advanced HIV disease and should receive the Advanced HIV package of care, which includes screening for cryptococcal antigen and TB-LAM.

The patient's CD4 count is 180 cells/mm³, which meets the criteria for receiving the Advanced HIV package of care. Table 52 in the National Integrated Tuberculosis Management Guidelines (2025), adults with a CD4 count ≤200 cells/ml should receive the Advanced HIV package of care, which includes screening for cryptococcal antigen and TB-LAM.
To the HIV guidelines, CrAg screening is recommended for PLHIV with CD4 ≤200 cell/ml. The patient has a CD4 count of 180 cells/mm³, which meets this criterion.

key_facts: [1] Adults living with HIV: start cotrimoxazole if WHO stage 3 or 4 or CD4 ≤350 cells/mm³, and for anyone with active TB regardless of CD4.
[1] Children under 5 years: all children under 5, regardless of WHO stage or CD4. From 5 years: WHO stage 3 or 4, CD4 ≤350, or a detectable viral load.
[1] HIV-exposed infants: start at 6 weeks (or at the first visit if later) and continue until HIV infection is ruled out and the baby is no longer breastfeeding.

question: Child living with HIV, 5 kg, starting first-line ART. Can I use the pALD (ABC/3TC/DTG 60/30/5 mg) dispersible tablet?
label: reason_first

blocks.text: The child weighs 5 kg, which is between 3-5.9 kg.

question: Breastfeeding mother of a 5-month-old has just tested HIV positive (new seroconversion). What do I do for the baby?
label: reason_first

blocks.text: The baby should be tested for HIV today and started on Enhanced Infant Prophylaxis (EIP) with AZT and NVP if under 6 weeks old, or just NVP if over 14 weeks old.
Start Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) on the mother right away.

notices: Verify doses, thresholds, contraindications, and patient-specific qualifications against the cited guideline passages before acting.

The baby should be tested for HIV today and started on Enhanced Infant Prophylaxis (EIP) with AZT and NVP if under 6 weeks old, or just NVP if over 14 weeks old.
